_meta.purpose: Equipment categories referenced by cut and recipe records (gear_category_refs / equipment_refs). This is the affiliate module inventory for the site: categories, not products. Products (ASINs, direct-merchant URLs, prices) live in a separate verified manifest that does not exist yet; nothing here is a product claim.
_meta.commission_note: Amazon category rates from the Standard Commission Income Statement read 2026-09-02 (source amazon-associates-commission-schedule). Rates change; the site never prints them. Recorded here only to rank build priority.
_meta.direct_program_note: direct_affiliate_candidates are brands to research, not enrolled programs. Portfolio rule: direct merchant beats network beats Amazon when economics and reputation justify it, and Amazon is never forced over a superior direct program.
_meta.placement_rule: Contextual only. A gear module appears where the record that references it renders: a probe on the brisket page, cedar planks on the salmon recipe. One to three items per module, never a wall. Amazon disclosure visible on every page that carries a Special Link.
_meta.offline_rule: No Amazon Special Link, Program Content or Amazon Mark in the PDF field guide, the KDP book or any printed poster (Associates Program Policies). Those surfaces point to pitlog.app pages instead.

ingredient_categories_note: Recipe shop_ingredient_categories (kosher-salt, coarse-black-pepper, apple-cider-vinegar, brown-sugar, molasses, smoked-paprika, honey, soy-sauce, maple-syrup, dijon-mustard, harissa and so on) are shelf-stable Grocery items at 1% plus a possible $1 first-Fresh-purchase bounty. They are worth building as a SHOP THIS RECIPE checklist because a recipe is a repeat shopping list, not because the rate is good. Fresh meat is never listed as available.
